corrections.why: The 1953-54 Coast and Geodetic Survey station description on the Forest Lookouts page gives the county as Trinity alone; only the Fire Lookout Association list names Shasta too. Human check needed.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The OpenStreetMap node we read has a name and a fire_lookout tag and an edit note about roads, but no status, so it does not show the tower standing. The Fire Lookout Association list marks the entry gone.

notes_for_editor: Read: the Forest Lookouts Slate Mountain page (1932 newspaper items as quoted there, 1944 and 1945 mentions, and the 1953-54 NGS station description and recovery note); the FFLA California list (Trinity row: Tower, Gone, no register ID); the OSM node (tags and edit note only); and the FFLOS page for the El Dorado County Slate Mountain (US 1893, CA 88). The El Dorado site is a different lookout and is not used for any fact here. Open items: (1) height: 26 ft in the 1932 Searchlight item versus about 45 ft in the 1953 NGS description; the record's 7.9 m (26 ft) is left out of facts and is not settled. (2) Agency and forest name: the 1954 note says property of the California State Forest Service; the September 1932 Dunsmuir News item says Shasta National Forest (the Searchlight item names no forest); the record says Trinity National Forest. No source here explains the change. (3) Status: 'gone' rests on one FFLA list row with no date, cause or register ID. No source describes the site today or whether it is open. The record's osm=standing conflict looks like an over-read of the OSM node. (4) Newspapers were read only as quoted on the Forest Lookouts page; the originals were not checked. A Peakbagging California lookout table appeared in search and was not read; it may give a status or note for this site.
